# reco_threat_detection_policy (Resource)

Manages a Reco threat detection (ITDR) policy that raises alerts on matching events.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "reco_threat_detection_policy" "admin_role_granted" {
  title                = "Administrator role granted"
  description          = "Alerts when a user is granted an administrator role."
  data_source          = "GSUITE_ADMIN_AUDIT_LOG_API"
  violation_risk_level = "MEDIUM"
  violation_risk_type  = "RISK_TYPE_USER"
  default_status       = "POLICY_STATUS_PREVIEW"
  conditions_jsonata   = "$.eventName = 'ASSIGN_ROLE' and $contains($.roleName, 'Admin')"
  description_template = "'Administrator role granted to ' & $.targetUser"
  how_to_remediate     = "Confirm the role assignment was approved and revoke it if not."
  tags                 = ["identity", "privilege"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `conditions_jsonata` (String) JSONata expression that evaluates to true when an event violates the policy. The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import.
- `data_source` (String) Data source whose events the policy evaluates, e.g. GSUITE_ADMIN_AUDIT_LOG_API. The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import.
- `description_template` (String) JSONata template producing the alert description (min 5 chars). The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import.
- `title` (String) Human-readable title (min 10 chars).
- `violation_risk_level` (String) Severity of a generated alert: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL. The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import.
- `violation_risk_type` (String) Risk category: RISK_TYPE_UNKNOWN, RISK_TYPE_DATA, RISK_TYPE_USER, RISK_TYPE_USER_TARGET, RISK_TYPE_USER_GROUP, or RISK_TYPE_APPLICATION. The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import.

### Optional

- `default_status` (String) Initial status for new instances: POLICY_STATUS_OFF, POLICY_STATUS_PREVIEW, or POLICY_STATUS_ON. The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import.
- `description` (String) Longer description shown in the Reco platform. The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import.
- `how_to_remediate` (String) Remediation guidance shown to operators. The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import.
- `tags` (List of String) Categorization tags.
- `why_should_i_care` (String) Business context explaining why this policy matters. The Reco API does not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected and it is empty after import.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Policy creation timestamp (read-only).
- `id` (String) Policy ID (stable UUID, set after create).
- `severity` (String) Severity returned by the API (read-only).
- `status` (String) Current policy status (read-only).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = reco_threat_detection_policy.admin_role_granted
  id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
}
```
